Dhamma

Dhammakitti_Mahāsāmi
Bud. C. 14th Cent. pupil of Dhammakitti; came to Ceylon from Yodhapura (Ayojjha ?) an. returned there an. lived in the Laṅkārāma, built by Paramarāja.
--Saddhammasaṅgaha. Pāli Chronicle on Buddhism in 11 chs. wrongly ascribed to Dhammakitti saṅgharāja.
See Malalasekera, Dict. Pāli Proper Names I. p. 1137; also Pāli Lit. of Ceylon p. 245.

Dhammakitti_Saṅgharāja
alias Devarakṣita alias Jayabāhu Mahāthera. Bud. patriarch of the Ceylonese Bud. Church; of monastery Saddhammatilaka of Gaḍaladeṇivihāra; pupil of Dhammakitti (a. of Pāramīmahāśataka); lived during the reigns of Kings Bhuvanekabāhu V an. Vīrabāhu III (1372-1410 A. D.). Held a synod of Bud. monks in 1369 to reform Buddhism in Ceylon. The Nikāyasaṅgraha in Sinhalese on the history of Buddhism is by him.
See Malalasekera, Pāli Lit. of Ceylon p.. 240. 242-45; also Dict. Pāli Proper Names I. p. 1137.
--Jinabodhāvali. Pāli.
--Bālāvatāra. Pāli. gr. in 7 chs. based on Kaccāyana. Colombo D. I. 2060-3. 2066.
Pt.. Hikkaduve Siri Sumangala. Colombo, 1894.
--Saṅkhepa. Pāli.
--Saddharmālaṅkāra. Pāli. on Bud. legends; a. enlarged transl. of Rasavāhinī of Vedeha Thera. See Malalasekera, ibid. p.. 226. 243 fn. 1. [Page231-a.

Dhammakitti
Sinhalese Bud. monk; pupil of Sāriputta; of Pulattipura (Polannaruva); 12th-13th Cent.; patronized by the minister Parakkama during the reign of Queen Līlāvatī.
--Dāṭhāvam3sa. Pāli. poem on the tooth relic based on older Sinhalese chronicle Daladāvam3sa.
See B. C. Law, His.. of Pāli Lit. p.. 579-81.
Pt.. JPTS. 1884, p. 109 ff. etc. See above p. 2a.

Dhammakitti
Bud. preceptor of Dhammakitti Mahāsāmi (a. of Saddhammasaṅgaha).
See Malalasekera, Dict. Pāli Proper Names I. p. 1137.

Dhammakitti
Ceylonese Bud. monk. of the monastery of Puṭabhattasela; lived a. Gaṅgāśrīpura (Gampola); during the reign of Bhuvanekabāhu I. (1277-88 A. D.); teacher of another Dhammakitti (a. of Saddharmālaṅkāra etc.).
--Pāramīmahāśataka. Pāli poem on ten perfections (Pāramitās).
See JRAS. 1896, p.. 202-3; Wint. HIL. II. p. 222; Malalasekera, Dict. Pāli Proper Names I. p. 1137.

Dhammakitti
Bud. came to Ceylon from Burma a. the invitation of King Parākramabāhu II (1236-68 A. D.); acc. to G. P. Malalasekera the a. hailed from South India.
--Cūḷavam3sa Pt. I. continuation of Mahāvam3sa. on the history of Ceylon from Mahāsena to Parākramabāhu II. Colombo D. I. 1908-12.
Diff. from the a. of Dāṭhāvam3sa. See W. Geiger, Pāli Lit. an. Language p. 44; G. P. Malalasekera, Pāli Lit. of Ceylon p.. 142. 215. [Page231-b]
Pt.. (1) Colombo, 1877. (2) PTS. 1935. in 2 vols.

Dhammacakkaṭīkā
one of the texts mentioned in a. inscription a. Pagan dated 1442 A. D. Prob. on Dhammacakkapavattanasutta.
See Pāli Lit. of Burma p. 105.

Dhammacakkappavattanasutta
or Dhammacakka or Dharmacakkasutta or Dhammacakkappavattana. Bud. Pāli. known a. ‘Sermon of Benares’; from Sam3yuttanikāya V. lvi. 11. See Malalasekera, Dict. Pāli Proper Names I. p.. 1138-39.
AMG. II. p.. 281. 288 AR. XX. p.. 479. 485. Br. Mus. Pāli. II. p.. 109. 139 (2 mss.). Colombo D. I. 283. Copen. Pāli p. 148. Fausboll 55 (several mss.). Kanjur Kyoto 747. Nanjio 657. 658.
Pt.. Sam3yuttanikāya V. p.. 360-63. Nālanda DNG Pāli Ser. Patna, 1959.
Q. by Nāgārjuna, in his Prajñāpāramitāśāstra. See IHQ. III. p. 415.
For a comparative study with the Tibetan Dharmacakrasūtra in the Kanjur see AMG. V. 111-21.
See Dharmacakraº below.
--C. Copen. Pāli p. 148.

Dhammacakkasutta
Bud. Pāli. from Aṅguttaranikāya. Colombo D. I. 171-73. 176. 179. 194-218. 220.

Dhammajjhāṇa

Dhammadāna
one of the texts mentioned in a. inscription a. Pagan dated 1442 A. D.

Dhammānanda
Bud. monk who wrote several Pāli gr. works. The Gandhavam3sa (p. 74) attributes to him the Kaccāyanasāra with its C., an. also the Kaccāyanabheda. [Page236-b]
See Malalasekera, Dict. Pāli Proper Names I. p. 1153.

Dhammapaññāpakaraṇa
Bud. Pāli. one of the texts mentioned in a. inscription a. Pagan dated 1442 A. D.
See Bode, Pāli Lit. of Burma p. 107.

Dhammapada
or Dharmapada. Bud. Collection of Buddhist ethical verses available in five versions.
For a detailed study an. comparison of diff. versions see B. C. Law, His.. of Pāli Lit. I. p.. 200-25; also J. Brough, Gāndhārī Dharmapada. Oxford, 1962.
--Bud. Pāli. from Khuddakanikāya of Suttapiṭaka. 423 verses in 26 vaggas.
See Rhys Davids. JRAS. 1900, p. 559 fn. Mentioned in Milindapanha. See Malalasekera, Dict. Pāli Proper Names I. p. 1144.
Br. Mus. Pāli p. 139 (2 mss.; 1 fr.). Colombo D. I. 75-77. 389. 391-92. 1698. 1768. Copen. Pāli p. 148 (2 mss.). Fausboll 67. 68. IO. Pāli p.. 60 (no. 17e). 74. (no. 32). Jesalmere p. 38 (fr.). Kandy II. p. 1. Oxf. Pāli p. 30. Paris Pāli p. 33 (2 mss.).
For a detailed account of the different sections of the work, of the edns. of the text etc. see Wint. HIL. II. p.. 80-84.
For a transl. into Skt. by the Indian Vanaratna (1384-1468 A. D.) in Ceylon see JBORS. XXI. i. p. 41. [Page232-b]
For a note on its name see Franke, ZDMG. 46 (1892) 734-36. On the 26 vaggas of the southern recension see H. Sumangala, Theosophist X (1888-89) 746-49. On the Turfan recension see R. Pischel. Sitzung. der Preuss. Ak. der Wiss. 1908, p.. 968-85.

Dhammapālathera
Bud. one of the foremost Pāli commentators; prob. a younger contemporary of Buddhaghoṣa (5th Cent.); resident of Badara (Padara) tittha in Damiḷa; must have studied a. Anurādhapura; Sāsanavam3sa (p. 33) an. Gandhavam3sa (p. 60) attribute 12 an. 13 works to him.
On Dhammapāla, his date an. works see G. P. Malalasekera, Pāli Lit. of Ceylon p.. 112-16; E. Hardy, ZDMG. 51 (1897) 105-27; Gandhavam3sa, JPTS. 1886, p.. 57. 60; Burlingame, HOS. 28. p.. 56 fn. 57 fn.; Wint. HIL. II. p.. 197 fn. 1 an. 205-6; B. C. Law, loc. cit. p.. 391-2 an. 481-516; J. of Sri Venk. Ori. Inst. II. p.. 347-52; Malalasekera, Dict. Pāli Proper Names I. p.. 1145-6.
